title: DC-area forecast: Higher humidity tonight, and heightened storm risk Thursday
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Clouds are more numerous this evening as temperatures slowly fall through the 80s.

What’s next? Storm threat returns for Thursday; some storms may be strong late. A couple more storms possible Friday, then a mainly sunny weekend.

Forecast in detail

Tonight: Partly cloudy overall. There is a chance for a passing shower or storm, mainly after midnight. Dew points rising deeper into the 60s keep temperatures from falling too much, with lows mainly in the upper 60s and lower 70s. Confidence: Medium-High

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Thursday): More like midsummer as humidity levels rise again and dew points head for the upper 60s or so. Moisture plus heat, as a weak front works this way, means showers and thunderstorms are possible. Some storms could be strong to severe, especially from late afternoon through evening. Before the storms, highs reach the mid- to upper 80s. Rain totals could reach an inch or so in heavier storms, but amount only to a few tenths or less in many spots. Confidence: Medium-High

Tomorrow night: Showers and storms are possible through the evening. Partly cloudy overnight with lows in the mid-60s to near 70. Some patchy fog late. Confidence: Medium-High

A look ahead

Partly sunny on Friday as humidity remains on the high side. We could see a couple late-day storms, but probably not as strong or numerous as Thursday. Highs again in the mid- and upper 80s. Confidence: Medium-High

Lots of sun this weekend. Saturday may be mainly in the mid-80s. By Sunday, readings rise to a range of mid-80s to around 90. For now, it looks dry both days. Confidence: Medium

Up around or above 90 to start the work week on Monday. We could stay hot through much or all of it. Confidence: Medium

DC weather history for August 26

A rare cold, rainy August day in 1908 set records, while later years brought heavy rain and severe thunderstorms that flooded roads and knocked out power across the region.

Today’s daily digit — 7/10: It could be worse. It could be better (see: the last few days). | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.
